 The Cougars remained in the top 10 of the latest CFP rankings Casey Lundquist | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source BYU running back Sione Moa against Baylor | BYU Photo In this story:
 BYU Cougars On Tuesday night, the BYU football program maintained a critical spot in the top 10 of the CFP rankings. If the season ended today, BYU would earn its first College Football Playoff berth in program history.
--> On Tuesday night, the BYU football program maintained a critical spot in the top 10 of the CFP rankings. If the season ended today, BYU would earn its first College Football Playoff berth in program history.
 Going into Tuesday's rankings, some BYU fans were concerned that Wake Forest and/or Texas Tech might leapfrog the Cougars after they earned signature road wins last weekend. Not only did they win, they looked dominant in the process.
--> Going into Tuesday's rankings, some BYU fans were concerned that Wake Forest and/or Texas Tech might leapfrog the Cougars after they earned signature road wins last weekend. Not only did they win, they looked dominant in the process.
 Instead, BYU maintained its no. 10 ranking while Wake Forest and Texas Tech landed at no. 11 and no. 12, respectively. After the rankings were revealed, CFP committee chair Hunter Yuracheck explained the separation between BYU, Wake Forest, and Texas Tech, even though BYU has on more loss.
--> Instead, BYU maintained its no. 10 ranking while Wake Forest and Texas Tech landed at no. 11 and no. 12, respectively. After the rankings were revealed, CFP committee chair Hunter Yuracheck explained the separation between BYU, Wake Forest, and Texas Tech, even though BYU has on more loss.
 "I think the biggest difference between those two teams is BYU's win over Notre Dame," Yuracheck said. "Wake Forest doesn't have the same type of win on their resume right now. That's going to be the separation between these teams."
--> "I think the biggest difference between those two teams is BYU's win over Notre Dame," Yuracheck said. "Wake Forest doesn't have the same type of win on their resume right now. That's going to be the separation between these teams."
 Yuracheck's comments appeared to indicate that not only was BYU's win over Notre Dame the reason it was ahead of the other two bubble teams this will, it's also the reason BYU will remain ahead of Wake Forest and Texas Tech in future rankings as long as it wins out. Wake Forest and Texas Tech won't have a chance to earn a top 10 win over the last two weeks of the season.
--> Yuracheck's comments appeared to indicate that not only was BYU's win over Notre Dame the reason it was ahead of the other two bubble teams this will, it's also the reason BYU will remain ahead of Wake Forest and Texas Tech in future rankings as long as it wins out. Wake Forest and Texas Tech won't have a chance to earn a top 10 win over the last two weeks of the season.
 In addition to Yuracheck's direct comments about BYU, he also commented on the rest of the CFP bubble.
--> In addition to Yuracheck's direct comments about BYU, he also commented on the rest of the CFP bubble.
 “I think the committee has a great deal of respect for Texas Tech and Wake Forest, and there is some separation in the minds of the committee between who’s at 12 and who’s at 13,” Yurachek said.
--> “I think the committee has a great deal of respect for Texas Tech and Wake Forest, and there is some separation in the minds of the committee between who’s at 12 and who’s at 13,” Yurachek said.
 Yuracheck's coments are important, because the Oregon Ducks are ranked 13th followed by Ohio State at 14. In the eyes of the committee, there is "separation" between the 12 (Texas Tech) and 13 (Oregon). If you piece Yuracheck's comments together, you can conclude two things about BYU's standing in the CFP rankings:

 While Yuracheck's comments are very encouraging for BYU's at-large hopes, the Cougars still don't control their destiny. If nobody loses in front of BYU, and Wake Forest and Texas Tech win their conference championships, BYU would be the first team out of the 12-team field.
--> While Yuracheck's comments are very encouraging for BYU's at-large hopes, the Cougars still don't control their destiny. If nobody loses in front of BYU, and Wake Forest and Texas Tech win their conference championships, BYU would be the first team out of the 12-team field.
 BYU either needs Miami, Indiana, or Tennessee to lose one of its last two games OR Texas Tech or Wake Forest to lose the conference championship game.
--> BYU either needs Miami, Indiana, or Tennessee to lose one of its last two games OR Texas Tech or Wake Forest to lose the conference championship game.
